title: Composition isomorphisms of derived inverse images and their coherence
statement:
Let $u:Y\to X$, $v:Z\to Y$, $w:W\to Z$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with the sheaf-level inverse images on abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], their composition isomorphisms $c_{u,v}:v^{-1}u^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(u\circ v)^{-1}$ and identity isomorphisms $e_X:\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], and the inverse images $u^{-1}:\Dplus(X_{\Et})\to\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$ on the bounded below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], with $\varphi_{u,K^\bullet}:u^{-1}(QK^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(u^{-1}K^\bullet)$ for bounded below complexes $K^\bullet$.

1. (Sheaf level.) $c$ and $e$ are associative and unital: $c_{u,v\circ w}\circ(c_{v,w}u^{-1})=c_{u\circ v,w}\circ(w^{-1}c_{u,v}):w^{-1}v^{-1}u^{-1}\to(u\circ v\circ w)^{-1}$, $c_{\mathrm{id}_X,u}=u^{-1}e_X:u^{-1}\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}\to u^{-1}$ and $c_{u,\mathrm{id}_Y}=e_Yu^{-1}:\mathrm{id}_Y^{-1}u^{-1}\to u^{-1}$.
2. (Derived level.) There are unique natural isomorphisms $c^D_{u,v}:v^{-1}u^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(u\circ v)^{-1}$ of functors $\Dplus(X_{\Et})\to\Dplus(Z_{\Et})$ and $e^D_X:\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ on $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ whose components at $QK^\bullet$ are, after the identifications $\varphi$, the classes $Q((c_{u,v,K^r})_r)$ and $Q((e_{X,K^r})_r)$ of the termwise isomorphisms, i.e. $\varphi_{u\circ v,K^\bullet}\circ c^D_{u,v,QK^\bullet}=Q((c_{u,v,K^r})_r)\circ\varphi_{v,u^{-1}K^\bullet}\circ v^{-1}(\varphi_{u,K^\bullet})$ and $e^D_{X,QK^\bullet}=Q((e_{X,K^r})_r)\circ\varphi_{\mathrm{id}_X,K^\bullet}$.
3. (Derived coherence.) $c^D,e^D$ satisfy the identities of (1) with $c,e$ replaced by $c^D,e^D$.

proof.text: **Step 1 (sheaf level: associativity).** Notation of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]: units $\eta_s$ of $s^{-1}\dashv s_*$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], isomorphisms $d_{s,t}:(st)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}s_*t_*$ and $d_S:(\mathrm{id}_S)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$, and for every composable pair $(s,t)$ the *unit equation* $(E_{s,t})$: $s_*t_*(c_{s,t,G})\circ s_*(\eta_{t,s^{-1}G})\circ\eta_{s,G}=d_{s,t,(st)^{-1}G}\circ\eta_{st,G}$, whose solution among isomorphisms $v^{-1}u^{-1}\to(uv)^{-1}$ is unique (clause (2)). Put $\alpha=c_{u,vw}\circ(c_{v,w}u^{-1})$, $\beta=c_{uv,w}\circ(w^{-1}c_{u,v})$ and $\gamma=\beta\circ(c_{v,w}u^{-1})^{-1}:(vw)^{-1}u^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(uvw)^{-1}$. We show that $\gamma$ satisfies $(E_{u,vw})$; by uniqueness $\gamma=c_{u,vw}$, i.e. $\beta=\alpha$. Fix $G$ on $X_{\Et}$, $H=u^{-1}G$. (a) $(E_{v,w})$ at $H$ gives $\eta_{vw,H}=d_{v,w}^{-1}\circ v_*w_*(c_{v,w,H})\circ v_*(\eta_{w,v^{-1}H})\circ\eta_{v,H}$. (b) Insert this into the left side of $(E_{u,vw})$ for $\gamma$ and move $u_*(vw)_*(\gamma_G)$ past $u_*(d_{v,w}^{-1})$ by naturality of $d_{v,w}$: the left side becomes $u_*(d^{-1}_{v,w})\circ u_*v_*w_*(\gamma_G\circ c_{v,w,H})\circ u_*v_*(\eta_{w,v^{-1}H})\circ u_*(\eta_{v,H})\circ\eta_{u,G}$, with $\gamma_G\circ c_{v,w,H}=\beta_G=c_{uv,w,G}\circ w^{-1}(c_{u,v,G})$. (c) Naturality of $\eta_w$ for $c_{u,v,G}$: $w_*w^{-1}(c_{u,v,G})\circ\eta_{w,v^{-1}H}=\eta_{w,(uv)^{-1}G}\circ c_{u,v,G}$; then $(E_{u,v})$ replaces $u_*v_*(c_{u,v,G})\circ u_*(\eta_{v,H})\circ\eta_{u,G}$ by $d_{u,v}\circ\eta_{uv,G}$. The left side is now $u_*(d^{-1}_{v,w})\circ u_*v_*w_*(c_{uv,w,G})\circ u_*v_*(\eta_{w,(uv)^{-1}G})\circ d_{u,v}\circ\eta_{uv,G}$. (d) Naturality of $d_{u,v}$ (for the morphisms $\eta_{w,(uv)^{-1}G}$ and $w_*(c_{uv,w,G})$) moves $d_{u,v}$ to the left: $u_*(d^{-1}_{v,w})\circ(d_{u,v}w_*)\circ(uv)_*w_*(c_{uv,w,G})\circ(uv)_*(\eta_{w,(uv)^{-1}G})\circ\eta_{uv,G}$, and $(E_{uv,w})$ turns the last three factors into $d_{uv,w}\circ\eta_{uvw,G}$. (e) By the associativity of $d$ [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-composition-coherence] (1), $u_*(d^{-1}_{v,w})\circ(d_{u,v}w_*)\circ d_{uv,w}=d_{u,vw}$ (at $(uvw)^{-1}G$). So the left side is $d_{u,vw}\circ\eta_{uvw,G}$, the right side of $(E_{u,vw})$. Hence $c_{u,v\circ w}\circ(c_{v,w}u^{-1})=c_{u\circ v,w}\circ(w^{-1}c_{u,v})$.

proof.text: **Step 2 (sheaf level: unit laws).** Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] gives, with naturality of $d_X$ ($(\mathrm{id}_X)_*(m)=d_X^{-1}\circ m\circ d_X$ for every morphism $m$), $(\mathrm{id}_X)_*(e_{X,G})\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id}_X,G}=d_{X,G}^{-1}\circ e_{X,G}\circ d_{X,\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}G}\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id}_X,G}=d_{X,G}^{-1}$ $(\ast)$. (a) $c_{\mathrm{id}_X,u}=u^{-1}e_X$: the candidate $\gamma_G=u^{-1}(e_{X,G})$ satisfies $(E_{\mathrm{id}_X,u})$: by naturality of $\eta_u$ for $e_{X,G}$, $(\mathrm{id}_X)_*u_*u^{-1}(e_{X,G})\circ(\mathrm{id}_X)_*(\eta_{u,\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}G})\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id}_X,G}=(\mathrm{id}_X)_*(\eta_{u,G})\circ(\mathrm{id}_X)_*(e_{X,G})\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id}_X,G}$, which by $(\ast)$ and naturality of $d_X$ is $d^{-1}_{X,u_*u^{-1}G}\circ\eta_{u,G}$; by the unit law [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-composition-coherence] (2), $d_{\mathrm{id}_X,u}=(d_Xu_*)^{-1}$, so this is $d_{\mathrm{id}_X,u,u^{-1}G}\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id}_X\circ u,G}$, the right side ($\mathrm{id}_X\circ u=u$). By uniqueness in clause (2), $c_{\mathrm{id}_X,u}=u^{-1}e_X$. (b) $c_{u,\mathrm{id}_Y}=e_Yu^{-1}$: for $\gamma_G=e_{Y,H}$, $H=u^{-1}G$, the left side of $(E_{u,\mathrm{id}_Y})$ is $u_*\bigl((\mathrm{id}_Y)_*(e_{Y,H})\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id}_Y,H}\bigr)\circ\eta_{u,G}=u_*(d^{-1}_{Y,H})\circ\eta_{u,G}$ by $(\ast)$ on $Y$, and $u_*(d_Y^{-1})=d_{u,\mathrm{id}_Y}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-composition-coherence] (2); this is the right side $d_{u,\mathrm{id}_Y,H}\circ\eta_{u,G}$. By uniqueness, $c_{u,\mathrm{id}_Y}=e_Yu^{-1}$. This proves (1).

proof.text: **Step 3 (the derived isomorphisms on $D$).** For $s\in\{u,v,uv,\mathrm{id}_X\}$ let $s^{-1}_D$ be the functor on the unbounded derived categories induced termwise, with the natural isomorphism $\varphi_{s,K}:s^{-1}_D(QK)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(s^{-1}K)$ for every complex $K$, natural in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]; $Q$ is a localization at the quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Since $c_{u,v}$ and $e_X$ are natural, their components form isomorphisms of complexes $c_{u,v,K}=(c_{u,v,K^r})_r:v^{-1}u^{-1}K\to(uv)^{-1}K$ and $e_{X,K}=(e_{X,K^r})_r:\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}K\to K$, natural in $K$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] (2) with $L=Q$, $F_1=Q\circ(v^{-1}u^{-1})$ (termwise composite), $F_1'=v^{-1}_D\circ u^{-1}_D$, $\phi_{1,K}=\varphi_{v,u^{-1}K}\circ v^{-1}_D(\varphi_{u,K})$, $F_2=Q\circ(uv)^{-1}$, $F_2'=(uv)^{-1}_D$, $\phi_2=\varphi_{uv}$, $\tau=Q(c_{u,v,-})$ ($F_1,F_2$ invert quasi-isomorphisms, being isomorphic to $F_i'\circ Q$): there is a unique natural transformation $c^D_{u,v}:v^{-1}_Du^{-1}_D\to(uv)^{-1}_D$ with $c^D_{u,v,QK}=\varphi_{uv,K}^{-1}\circ Q(c_{u,v,K})\circ\varphi_{v,u^{-1}K}\circ v^{-1}_D(\varphi_{u,K})$, an isomorphism since $\tau$ is. Likewise, with $F_1=Q\circ\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}$, $F_1'=(\mathrm{id}_X^{-1})_D$, $\phi_1=\varphi_{\mathrm{id}_X}$, $F_2=Q$, $F_2'=\mathrm{id}$, $\phi_2=\mathrm{id}$, $\tau=Q(e_{X,-})$: a unique natural isomorphism $e^D_X:(\mathrm{id}_X^{-1})_D\to\mathrm{id}$ with $e^D_{X,QK}=Q(e_{X,K})\circ\varphi_{\mathrm{id}_X,K}$. These are the formulas of (2).

proof.text: **Step 4 (restriction to $\Dplus$; existence and uniqueness in (2)).** The inverse images on $\Dplus$ are the restrictions of the $s^{-1}_D$ to the full subcategories $\Dplus$, which they preserve [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]; so $v^{-1}u^{-1}$, $(uv)^{-1}$ and $\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}$ on $\Dplus$ are restrictions of $v^{-1}_Du^{-1}_D$, $(uv)^{-1}_D$, $(\mathrm{id}_X^{-1})_D$, and the components of $c^D_{u,v}$, $e^D_X$ of Step 3 at objects of $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ are morphisms of the full subcategory $\Dplus(Z_{\Et})$, resp. $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$. Their restrictions are natural isomorphisms on $\Dplus$ with the components of (2) at $QK$, $K$ bounded below ($QK\in\Dplus$). Uniqueness: if $\sigma,\sigma'$ are natural transformations of functors on $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ agreeing at every $QK$ with $K$ bounded below, then for any $M\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ choose an isomorphism $i:M\xrightarrow{\sim}QI$ with $I$ a bounded below complex [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]; naturality gives $\sigma_M=G_2(i)^{-1}\circ\sigma_{QI}\circ G_1(i)=\sigma'_M$ ($G_1,G_2$ the source and target functors). So $c^D_{u,v}$, $e^D_X$ on $\Dplus$ are unique with the components of (2).

proof.text: **Step 5 (derived associativity).** Work on $D$ with Step 3's transformations; the identity on $\Dplus$ is its restriction (Step 4). Both sides $A=c^D_{u,vw}\circ(c^D_{v,w}u^{-1}_D)$ and $B=c^D_{uv,w}\circ(w^{-1}_Dc^D_{u,v})$ are natural transformations $w^{-1}_Dv^{-1}_Du^{-1}_D\to(uvw)^{-1}_D$. Fix a complex $K$ and put $\Phi_K=\varphi_{w,v^{-1}u^{-1}K}\circ w^{-1}_D(\varphi_{v,u^{-1}K})\circ w^{-1}_Dv^{-1}_D(\varphi_{u,K})$. (a) By naturality of $c^D_{v,w}$ for the isomorphism $\varphi_{u,K}:u^{-1}_D(QK)\to Q(u^{-1}K)$ and Step 3 at the complex $u^{-1}K$, $c^D_{v,w,u^{-1}_DQK}=(vw)^{-1}_D(\varphi_{u,K})^{-1}\circ\varphi_{vw,u^{-1}K}^{-1}\circ Q(c_{v,w,u^{-1}K})\circ\Phi_K$; composing with $c^D_{u,vw,QK}=\varphi_{uvw,K}^{-1}\circ Q(c_{u,vw,K})\circ\varphi_{vw,u^{-1}K}\circ(vw)^{-1}_D(\varphi_{u,K})$ gives $A_{QK}=\varphi^{-1}_{uvw,K}\circ Q(c_{u,vw,K}\circ c_{v,w,u^{-1}K})\circ\Phi_K$. (b) $w^{-1}_D(c^D_{u,v,QK})=w^{-1}_D(\varphi_{uv,K})^{-1}\circ w^{-1}_DQ(c_{u,v,K})\circ w^{-1}_D(\varphi_{v,u^{-1}K}\circ v^{-1}_D\varphi_{u,K})$, and naturality of $\varphi_w$ in the complex for $c_{u,v,K}$ gives $\varphi_{w,(uv)^{-1}K}\circ w^{-1}_DQ(c_{u,v,K})=Q(w^{-1}c_{u,v,K})\circ\varphi_{w,v^{-1}u^{-1}K}$; composing with $c^D_{uv,w,QK}=\varphi^{-1}_{uvw,K}\circ Q(c_{uv,w,K})\circ\varphi_{w,(uv)^{-1}K}\circ w^{-1}_D(\varphi_{uv,K})$ gives $B_{QK}=\varphi^{-1}_{uvw,K}\circ Q(c_{uv,w,K}\circ w^{-1}c_{u,v,K})\circ\Phi_K$. (c) By Step 1 in each degree, $c_{u,vw,K}\circ c_{v,w,u^{-1}K}=c_{uv,w,K}\circ w^{-1}c_{u,v,K}$ as morphisms of complexes, so $A_{QK}=B_{QK}$ for every complex $K$, and $A=B$ by the uniqueness clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] ($L=Q$).

proof.text: **Step 6 (derived unit laws).** As in Step 5, on $D$ then restricted. (a) $c^D_{\mathrm{id}_X,u}=u^{-1}e^D_X$: at $QK$, $u^{-1}_D(e^D_{X,QK})=u^{-1}_D(Q(e_{X,K}))\circ u^{-1}_D(\varphi_{\mathrm{id}_X,K})$, and naturality of $\varphi_u$ for $e_{X,K}$ gives $u^{-1}_D(Q(e_{X,K}))=\varphi_{u,K}^{-1}\circ Q(u^{-1}e_{X,K})\circ\varphi_{u,\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}K}$; so $u^{-1}_D(e^D_{X,QK})=\varphi^{-1}_{u,K}\circ Q(u^{-1}e_{X,K})\circ\varphi_{u,\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}K}\circ u^{-1}_D(\varphi_{\mathrm{id}_X,K})$, which is $c^D_{\mathrm{id}_X,u,QK}$ (Step 3) because $c_{\mathrm{id}_X,u,K}=u^{-1}e_{X,K}$ degreewise (Step 2). (b) $c^D_{u,\mathrm{id}_Y}=e^D_Yu^{-1}$: by naturality of $e^D_Y$ for $\varphi_{u,K}$, $e^D_{Y,u^{-1}_DQK}=\varphi_{u,K}^{-1}\circ e^D_{Y,Q(u^{-1}K)}\circ(\mathrm{id}_Y^{-1})_D(\varphi_{u,K})=\varphi_{u,K}^{-1}\circ Q(e_{Y,u^{-1}K})\circ\varphi_{\mathrm{id}_Y,u^{-1}K}\circ(\mathrm{id}_Y^{-1})_D(\varphi_{u,K})$, which is $c^D_{u,\mathrm{id}_Y,QK}$ because $c_{u,\mathrm{id}_Y,K}=e_{Y,u^{-1}K}$ degreewise (Step 2). In both cases the two transformations agree on every $QK$, hence are equal by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] (3); restricting to $\Dplus$ (Step 4) gives (3).
